request: Write a shot brief for a 6-second product clip reusing the 'slow dolly-in' camera tag from a brief that worked on a different text-to-video model.
expected: checks the target model's current documentation for its actual supported camera-control vocabulary before reusing the tag
falls back to plain compositional language for framing if the tag is not confirmed for the target model
treats resulting camera behavior as best-effort, not a guaranteed controllable parameter
must_not: assume a camera-motion tag documented for one provider transfers to a different model without checking
promise the exact framing described will be reproduced
review_evidence: citation or note confirming the target model's documented camera-control feature set
the exact tag/phrasing used in the final brief, distinguished from the reused one

request: Review a product tour where a settings modal always fades in centered on screen, regardless of which of several icons the user tapped to open it.
expected: flags the missing positional link between the trigger icon and the modal's entrance
recommends animating the modal's entrance from the tapped icon's on-screen position or nearest edge
distinguishes the modal's foreground motion from the backdrop's recede
must_not: recommend a blanket camera zoom on every icon tap as the fix
leave the fix as a generic center fade with no positional relationship to the trigger
review_evidence: frame comparison of each icon's screen position against the modal's entrance origin
note of which specific icons were tested

request: An ad's on-screen rep counter jumps from one number to the next with zero in-between frames and viewers say it looks broken.
expected: identifies missing spacing (no velocity curve) between digit changes as the cause, not a frame-rate problem
adds a short eased scale or crossfade between digit states
sizes the added ease to stay brisk, matching a fast countdown rather than slowing it down
must_not: recommend simply lengthening total duration without adding any spacing curve
apply a heavy, slow ease that undermines the countdown's brisk pace
review_evidence: before/after frame sequence around one digit change showing the added in-between frames

request: Draft a brief for an animated spokesperson explainer whose mouth 'naturally lip-syncs' to the narration, for a render pipeline that has not been confirmed to support viseme mapping.
expected: checks whether the actual render pipeline has a confirmed lip-sync or viseme feature before the brief assumes it
rewrites the brief to use a neutral or generic non-synced mouth loop if the capability is unconfirmed
keeps the visual sequence able to communicate meaning independent of the narration audio
must_not: leave the brief asserting automatic lip-sync without confirming the pipeline supports it
assume any narrated character rig auto-syncs mouth movement to audio by default
review_evidence: confirmation (or lack thereof) from the specific pipeline's documentation about viseme/lip-sync support
the revised brief language describing the fallback mouth treatment

request: Plan cut points for a music video assembled from separately generated clips, timed to an existing track.
expected: pins each clip boundary to the track's verified beat markers from an actual detection or annotation pass
treats motion inside each generated clip as approximate, checked after generation rather than assumed frame-exact
documents the beat-detection evidence used, not an assumed tempo
must_not: guess beat placement from a nominal BPM without a verified beat grid
claim the generated clips' internal motion lands on-beat frame-exactly
review_evidence: the beat grid or waveform annotation the cut points were pinned against
note of which cuts, if any, needed adjustment after reviewing the generated clips against the beat grid

request: A review report for an ad states motion was checked 'at t=0:12 and t=0:34' using timecodes from the editing project's timeline, after the final export was re-encoded and trimmed.
expected: flags that authored timeline timecodes may not match the real presentation timestamps (PTS) of the delivered file after re-encoding/trimming
re-extracts frames from the actual delivered file at its own PTS
labels reported timestamps as coming from the specific delivered file, not the project timeline
must_not: accept authored-timeline timecodes as equivalent to the delivered file's real timestamps without checking for drift
report the review as covering moments that were never actually located in the real output
review_evidence: the measured drift/trim amount between timeline time and real file PTS
corrected timestamps sourced from the delivered file

request: A reviewer flags a keyboard-shortcut-triggered modal for using a fixed center-anchored fade instead of animating from a trigger position, the way pointer-triggered modals in the same tour do.
expected: recognizes the keyboard trigger has no on-screen contact point to originate an entrance animation from
retains the center-anchored appearance for this specific trigger type
states the evidence for retaining it: no visible pointer contact point exists for a keyboard-triggered action
must_not: invent an arbitrary on-screen origin point for a keyboard-triggered action that never touched the screen
force the keyboard-triggered modal to match the pointer-triggered modals' origin behavior for consistency alone
review_evidence: confirmation that the keyboard shortcut has no associated on-screen element or click position
explicit note that the center-anchored treatment was a deliberate retain, not an oversight

request: Trim 4 seconds off the head of a delivered clip and re-encode it to a smaller container; no motion, timing, or shot content is changing.
expected: recognizes this as a pure trim/re-encode task with no motion decision involved
completes the trim/re-encode without invoking motion-choreography judgment from this skill
must_not: apply timing/spacing, continuity, or motion-review judgment to a task that involves no motion decision
add easing, anticipation, or any other motion treatment that was not part of the original clip
review_evidence: confirmation that only trim points and container/codec changed, with no reference to motion timing
